_comment: Our language: the short list of words a person needs to follow a
conversation about Precedent. The one source for them -- the page
documentation/OUR_LANGUAGE.md is rendered from this file by
tools/our_language.py, and doc_sync.py fails if the two disagree.
Edit the words here, never on the page.

A word listed here is printed under "Our language" by the Vocabulary command (tools/precedent_vocabulary.py), and a practice's `command:` phrase that matches one moves there instead of the command list -- it names a thing, not an action.

`retired` lists words that are no longer ours, with what replaced them. precedent_check.py's retired-words check reads it and refuses a retired phrase in live text (practice: rename-updates-links), so retiring the next word is one entry here, not a new check. History is left alone: a practice's ## Story, text in quotation marks, todo/, decisions/, gotchas/, record/, evals/, and any document whose frontmatter says kind: record or a finished status (closed, executed, accepted, superseded, retired). A line that says it is about the retirement itself (retired, formerly, renamed, old name) is left alone too.

words.meaning: A rule. Each one is a single file holding the rule, the reason for it, and the story of how it came about.
The practices everyone gets. It is BestPractice's own collection, named `precedent`.
The practices just for you. Usually a repository named `precedent-individual`.
Practices a group of people share. A repository may use none, one, or several.
Every practice set in force for you: the universal set, your individual set, your shared sets, and the repo-local practices of the repository you are in.

Belonging to the repository you are working in -- your work repository, the one with BestPractice copied in. Its own practices, kept in its `local/` folder, are its repo-local practices, and apply only there.
A practice that actually applies here, right now.
Where a set of practices comes from, usually a repository.
Which kind of set a source is: universal, shared, individual, or repo-local.
The one shared branch regular work lands on. (A branch is a separate line of work in a repository.)
The branch your saved work lands on when you say "Go update": pre-staging if you use all three branch tiers, otherwise staging, or main.

The short-lived branch one session works on, on GitHub -- the kind named like `claude/<topic>-<random>`. GitHub's own word for it; some teams say "topic branch". It survives a lost session but is easy to forget, and it is deleted once its work is merged.
The three branches work climbs through, in that order. Pre-staging is where saved work waits, staging is where it is fully checked, and main is production -- what everyone gets.

One of the branches in the pre-staging, staging, main climb, or one of the two that travel with them: staging's old name `precedent-beta-v01` and Promote's lock branch `precedent-promote-lock`. A tier branch is never offered for deletion.
One of the five steps work climbs from idea to production: Consider, Act, Booked, Debut, Produce. "Promote 3" means stage 3, and each stage is read back before it runs.

retired.why: A set of practices is shared by whoever declares it, not owned by a team: one person can use several, and one set serves people on many teams. "team" meaning a group of people is still ordinary English and is not retired.
